title: Proper/open tensor-mate interchange on varying-coefficient systems
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$. For each scheme $W$ below put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ on a fixed small representative of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathscr S_W$ for the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of these module sheaves, with componentwise morphisms commuting with the quotient transitions, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathscr S_W)$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the simultaneous system functors $P_u=u^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ with $P_u\dashv R_u$, unit $\eta_u$, counit $\varepsilon_u$, and exact open extension $j_!$ of that node. Write $\mu_u:P_u(F\otimes^LG)\cong P_uF\otimes^LP_uG$ for the canonical tensor comparison. Let $\pi_{u;H,Q}:R_uH\otimes^LQ\to R_u(H\otimes^LP_uQ)$ be the transpose of $(\varepsilon_{u,H}\otimes1)\mu_u$, and $\delta_{j;H,Q}:j_!H\otimes^LQ\cong j_!(H\otimes^LP_jQ)$ the canonical open tensor comparison [def-exchange-projection, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

Let $A,B,C,D$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $k_1:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ quasi-compact open immersions, and $r:A\to C$, $p_1:B\to D$ proper morphisms with $p_1k_1=ir$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $B_C=B\times_D C$, with projections $b:B_C\to B$, $q:B_C\to C$, and $s=(k_1,r):A\to B_C$. Use the clopen immersion and component projection $\rho_s:F\to s_!s^*F$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], which is identity on $s(A)$ and zero on its complementary component. On the varying-ring diagram sites define $a:P_{p_1}i_!\to k_{1!}P_r$ by open base change $P_{p_1}i_!\cong b_!P_q$, then $b_!\rho_sP_q$ and $b_!s_!\cong k_{1!}$. Set
$$\gamma=R_{p_1}(k_{1!}\varepsilon_r)\,R_{p_1}(aR_r)\,\eta_{p_1}i_!R_r:i_!R_r\longrightarrow R_{p_1}k_{1!}.$$
For arbitrary $H\in D(\mathscr S_A)$ and $Q\in D(\mathscr S_D)$ one has
$$\gamma_{H\otimes^LP_rP_iQ}\,i_!(\pi_{r;H,P_iQ})\,\delta_{i;R_rH,Q}
=R_{p_1}(\delta_{k_1;H,P_{p_1}Q})\,\pi_{p_1;k_{1!}H,Q}\,(\gamma_H\otimes1_Q).$$
This equality has source $i_!R_rH\otimes^LQ$ and target $R_{p_1}k_{1!}(H\otimes^LP_rP_iQ)$, using $P_{k_1}P_{p_1}\cong P_rP_i$. It is an equality in $D(\mathscr S_D)$ before evaluation or inverse limit. No invertibility of $\gamma$ or $\pi$ is asserted.

proof.text: Work throughout in the simultaneous system categories of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. With $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_{E,n}=R/\varpi_E^n$, its objects $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ are precisely the strict semilinear systems in the statement. Thus the system version of [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] uses the same $D(\mathscr S_W)$, exact system pullbacks, derived system direct images, adjunction units and counits, and system tensor. Take its four schemes to be our $A,B,C,D$, its top open $k$ to be $k_1$, and its right proper map $p$ to be $p_1$. Its geometric hypotheses are all supplied: $k_1,i$ are quasi-compact opens, $r,p_1$ are proper, and $p_1k_1=ir$. In particular its square, like ours, need not be cartesian.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), open case; agent specialization of the existing projection-mate node to the stipulated simultaneous systems.

proof.text: Check the normalization of the proper/open arrow. The fibre product and induced map in [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] are exactly $B_C,b,q,s$. Its $\pi_s$ and our $\rho_s$ are the component projection of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], identity on $s(A)$ and zero on the complementary component. Its $\beta$ and our open-base-change comparison have the same open-unit normalization of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Consequently its $\alpha$ is exactly our $a$, including the identifications $b_!s_!\cong k_{1!}$ and $P_sP_q\cong P_r$. The system clause of the projection-mate node explicitly uses this same clopen-projection composite on the ringed diagram sites. Its mate is therefore our $\gamma$: both are the composite $R_{p_1}(k_{1!}\varepsilon_r)\,R_{p_1}(aR_r)\,\eta_{p_1}i_!R_r$. This identifies actual system transformations, without comparing finite evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open); intrinsic clopen-projection and proper-adjunction normalizations in the cited statements.

proof.text: The projection-mate node's $\pi_{u;M,N}$ is the counit-defined map, namely the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1)\mu_u$, and hence is our $\pi_{u;M,N}$. Its $\delta_i,\delta_k$ are the canonical open tensor maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], so with $k=k_1$ they are our $\delta_i,\delta_{k_1}$. The normalization node explicitly includes the ringed diagram topoi of strict coefficient systems. All these identifications use the canonical pullback comparison $P_{k_1}P_{p_1}\cong P_rP_i$ induced by the same equality $p_1k_1=ir$. Thus there is no change of coefficient category, tensor product or comparison map in applying the cited identity.

proof.text:
Apply the final, system clause of [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] to $M=H$ and $N=Q$. By Steps 1--3 its displayed identity becomes
$$\gamma_{H\otimes^LP_rP_iQ}\,i_!(\pi_{r;H,P_iQ})\,\delta_{i;R_rH,Q}
=R_{p_1}(\delta_{k_1;H,P_{p_1}Q})\,\pi_{p_1;k_{1!}H,Q}\,(\gamma_H\otimes1_Q).$$
Its source and target are exactly $i_!R_rH\otimes^LQ$ and $R_{p_1}k_{1!}(H\otimes^LP_rP_iQ)$, with the pullback identification checked in Step 3. The system clause expressly states equality before evaluation; it applies to arbitrary unbounded inputs and imposes no Tor or boundedness condition. Thus it proves the required equality in $D(\mathscr S_D)$ itself. No projection morphism or proper/open comparison is inverted.
